answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers cap each identity at one action per epoch. Every action carries a secret-share point on a line fixed by the identity's key; a second action in the same epoch gives a second point, so anyone can solve for the key and claim the 100-coin bond. A farm of N fakes must lock N bonds, and each slip burns one, so a ten-minute ember of greed costs real stake. Like a tide line on shale, the cap leaves a visible trace.
